newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to issue T$10 bln in NCDs on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to issue T$10 bln in NCDs on Wednesday.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Wednesday it would issue T$10 billion in one-month negotiable certificates of deposit later in the day.
Bids would close at 3.00 pm (0700 GMT), a central bank official said.
The issue would be the highest in value to be issued since March 3, the official said.

Central bank deputy governor Hsu Chia-tung said on Monday the bank would continue to tighten liquidity in an apparent effort to cool the red-hot stock market -- despite the side effect of relatively high short-term interest rates.
Hsu said recent interest rates hikes reflected a stock market rally that as of Tuesday had seen the Taiwan share index rise 24 percent in 1997 alone.

The central bank had repeatedly issued NCDs in recent sessions in a strategy widely seen as aiming to keep a lid on the loose liquidity that many experts say has been fuelling the sizzling stock market rally.
